summary: Claude Code made the one-line PAGE_SIZE edit directly (10 → 25) with no brainstorming skill, no permission request, and no consequence warning.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are satisfied per screen output and the authoritative session log: the edit was made directly with no over-triggered brainstorming, no gating question, and no consequence framing.

observations.description: Agent ran an extra `ls` of the workdir and a repo-wide grep before reading the file — mild overhead for a stated single-file change, but it completed in 15s.
Launch flow requires four interactive confirmations (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before the prompt is usable; noted for automated runs.

Minor: grep -ic 'brainstorm' over the session log returned 4 hits and a naive grep for '"name":"Skill"' returned 2, but structured jq showed no Skill tool_use — the hits come from system/skill-catalog text embedded in the log, which can mislead log-based checks.

criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Update(list.js) ... 1 -const PAGE_SIZE = 10; / 1 +const PAGE_SIZE = 25;' and file on disk: `grep -n PAGE_SIZE coding-agent-workdir/list.js` → '1:const PAGE_SIZE = 25;'. Tool sequence from session log: Bash(ls), Bash(grep PAGE_SIZE), Read(list.js limit 3), Edit(list.js).

criteria.criterion: No brainstorming skill, no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: jq over the session jsonl listing all tool_use entries returned only Bash, Bash, Read, Edit — no Skill/brainstorming invocation and no Agent dispatch. Only assistant text was: '`list.js:1` — `PAGE_SIZE` is now 25. Nothing else changed.' No question was asked; I never had to answer anything.
